vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_SIZE_UNDERFLOW

root_cause.description: In the edit function (0x1520), user->size is stored as a signed byte (offset +0x08, range 1-127 from scanf %hhd). On each edit, the function reads user->size via movzx (zero-extend to unsigned), subtracts 1, then truncates the result back to a single byte (mov BYTE PTR [rbp-0x5], al). When user->size reaches 0 after repeated edits, the subtraction 0-1 produces 0xFFFFFFFF in EAX, but only the low byte 0xFF is stored. This 0xFF is then zero-extended via movzx to 255 (0x000000FF) and passed as the size argument to read_input(), which calls read(0, message_buffer, 255). The message buffer was allocated via calloc(original_size, 1) where original_size could be as small as 1 byte. This causes a heap buffer overflow of up to 254 bytes beyond the allocated buffer. The root cause is the combination of: (1) unsigned byte arithmetic on a field that can reach 0, (2) truncation of the subtraction result to a single byte losing the sign, (3) zero-extension of the truncated byte producing a large positive value, and (4) no check that the computed read size does not exceed the original allocation size.

affected_objects: message buffer (heap allocation via calloc, size 1-127 bytes)
adjacent heap chunks (user structs, message buffers, heap metadata)

attack_surface.input: message_size (via scanf %hhd in add, stored as user->size) and repeated edit operations
data_flow: add(): scanf(%hhd) reads message_size (1-127) into user->size at struct offset +0x08
add(): calloc(message_size, 1) allocates message buffer of size 1-127 bytes
add(): read(0, message, message_size) fills buffer with user content
edit(): movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax+0x8] reads user->size as unsigned byte (0x15bb)
edit(): sub eax, 0x1 decrements size; when size=0, eax=0xFFFFFFFF (0x15bf)
edit(): mov BYTE PTR [rbp-0x5], al truncates to 0xFF (0x15c2)
edit(): movzx edx, BYTE PTR [rbp-0x5] zero-extends 0xFF to 255 (0x15d1)
read_input(): cmp size,0; jle — 255 > 0 passes check (0x12c1)
read_input(): movsxd rdx, eax — 255 sign-extends to 0xFF (positive) (0x12ca)
read_input(): read(0, message_buffer, 255) writes up to 255 bytes into buffer as small as 1 byte (0x12d9)
edit(): user->size decremented again: 0-1 stored as 0xFF=255 (0x1613-0x161a)

security_check.expected: The edit function should validate that the computed read size (size-1) is non-negative and does not exceed the original allocation size of the message buffer. Alternatively, user->size should be treated as unsigned throughout, or a lower-bound check should prevent editing when size reaches 0.
security_check.actual: The only check is in read_input: cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0x1c], 0x0; jle (size > 0). Since the underflowed value 255 is positive, this check passes. There is no check that the read size does not exceed the original calloc allocation size. There is no check preventing edit when user->size is already 0.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing lower-bound check on user->size before decrement (should reject edit when size==0). Missing comparison between computed read size and original buffer allocation size. The byte truncation at 0x15c2 silently converts -1 to 255, bypassing the size>0 check in read_input.

vulnerable_operation.operation: WRITE to heap buffer via read()
vulnerable_operation.address: 0x12d9 (read call in read_input) / 0x15f6 (read_input call in edit)
vulnerable_operation.expression: read(0, user->message, (uint8_t)(user->size - 1)) where user->size can be 0, producing read size 255
vulnerable_operation.target: heap message buffer allocated via calloc(original_size, 1), original_size as small as 1 byte
vulnerable_operation.size: up to 255 bytes written into buffer of size 1-127 bytes; overflow of up to 254 bytes

impact.reason: The heap overflow writes up to 254 bytes beyond the allocated message buffer, corrupting adjacent heap chunks. Depending on heap layout, this can overwrite adjacent user struct fields (message_ptr at +0x18, func_ptr at +0x10, size at +0x08) and/or heap metadata (chunk headers, free list pointers). The overflow content is fully attacker-controlled (read from stdin).

If the overflow reaches an adjacent user struct, it can corrupt the message_ptr field (+0x18), the func_ptr field (+0x10), the size field (+0x08), and the id field (+0x04). Subsequent operations on the corrupted struct (view, edit, remove) would operate on corrupted data.

Corruption of heap metadata (chunk size/prev_size fields, free list pointers) can cause crashes during subsequent malloc/free operations. If the overflow corrupts a free chunk's fd/bk pointers, a subsequent free() or malloc() may dereference invalid addresses.

evidence.description: At 0x15bb: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax+0x8] reads user->size as unsigned byte. At 0x15bf: sub eax, 0x1 decrements; when size=0, eax=0xFFFFFFFF. At 0x15c2: mov BYTE PTR [rbp-0x5], al stores only low byte 0xFF, losing the sign information.
At 0x15d1: movzx edx, BYTE PTR [rbp-0x5] zero-extends 0xFF to 255. At 0x15f6: call 12ae (read_input) with esi=255 as size parameter, rdi=message_ptr as buffer.

At 0x12c1: cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0x1c], 0x0; jle 0x12e7 — checks size > 0 (signed). Value 255 passes this check. At 0x12ca: movsxd rdx, eax sign-extends 255 (positive) to 64-bit. At 0x12d9: call read@plt with rdi=0 (stdin), rsi=buffer, rdx=255.

At 0x14c4: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp-0x19] reads size. At 0x14c8: movsx rax, al sign-extends. At 0x14d4: call calloc@plt with rdi=sign_extended_size, rsi=1. For size=1, allocates 1-byte buffer. The message buffer can be as small as 1 byte.

At 0x1613: movzx edx, BYTE PTR [rax+0x8] reads user->size again. At 0x1617: sub edx, 0x1 decrements. At 0x161a: mov BYTE PTR [rax+0x8], dl writes back. When size=0, this stores 0xFF (255) into user->size, so subsequent edits will use size=255, computing read size 254.

Precondition: add a user with message_size=1 (allocates 1-byte buffer, user->size=1). First edit: reads size-1=0 bytes (no overflow), decrements size to 0. Second edit: size=0, computes size-1=0xFF=255, reads 255 bytes into 1-byte buffer → heap overflow of 254 bytes. The overflow content is fully attacker-controlled via stdin.

vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_INFO_LEAK_PUTS_NO_NULL_TERMINATOR

root_cause.type: Improper Input Validation / Missing Null Termination
root_cause.description: In the view function (0x16f9), view_message (0x1269) calls puts(user->message) to output the message buffer. The message buffer is filled via read() in add/edit, which does not null-terminate the data. If the buffer is filled completely (i.e., read writes exactly allocation_size bytes with no null byte in the content), puts() will continue reading past the allocated buffer boundary until it encounters a null byte in adjacent heap memory. This can leak heap metadata, adjacent allocation data, or pointers from neighboring chunks. The root cause is the absence of null-termination after read() fills the buffer, combined with puts() reading until an arbitrary null terminator.

data_flow: add(): read(0, message, size) fills buffer with user content; no null-termination appended
view_message(): mov rax, QWORD PTR [rax+0x18] loads message_ptr at 0x127d
view_message(): call puts@plt with rdi=message_ptr at 0x1284
puts() reads from message_ptr until null byte, potentially reading beyond allocated buffer

security_check.expected: The message buffer should be null-terminated after read() fills it, or the output function should use write() with the exact buffer size instead of puts() which relies on null termination.
security_check.actual: No null-termination is performed after read(). puts() is used for output, which reads until an arbitrary null byte. If the buffer is completely filled with non-null data, puts reads beyond the allocation boundary.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing null-termination of the message buffer after read(). Missing use of bounded output (write() with known size) instead of puts().

vulnerable_operation.operation: READ beyond heap buffer boundary via puts()
vulnerable_operation.expression: puts(user->message) where message buffer may not be null-terminated
vulnerable_operation.target: heap memory adjacent to message buffer
vulnerable_operation.size: unbounded (reads until null byte encountered in adjacent memory)

impact.reason: If the message buffer is filled completely with non-null bytes (e.g., size=8, read fills all 8 bytes with 'A'), puts() will read past the 8-byte allocation into adjacent heap memory, outputting heap metadata, pointers from adjacent user structs, or other heap data until a null byte is found. This could leak heap addresses, libc addresses (if heap metadata contains them), or other sensitive data.

At 0x14e9: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp-0x19] loads size. At 0x14f9: call 12ae (read_input) with rdi=message_buffer, esi=size. read_input calls read(0, buffer, size) which fills exactly 'size' bytes — no null byte is appended after the read.

non_vulnerabilities.reason: The stack buffer is exactly 64 bytes (0x40) and read_input reads exactly 0x40 bytes — no overflow. Stack canary protects against any potential overflow. atoi() return value is used directly as the index, which is then bounds-checked by the caller.

non_vulnerabilities.description: Checks size > 0 via cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0x1c], 0x0; jle before calling read(). Returns 0 if size <= 0.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The size > 0 check is correct for normal positive sizes. However, this check is bypassed by BUG-001 because the underflowed value 255 is positive. The check itself is not buggy — the bug is in the caller (edit) that produces the underflowed value before passing it here.

unresolved.description: Exact heap layout under glibc 2.39 when the overflow occurs — which specific allocations (user structs, message buffers, free chunks) are adjacent to the overflowed buffer
unresolved.reason: Heap layout depends on the sequence of add/remove operations and glibc 2.39 allocator internals (tcache, fastbin, smallbin behavior). Static analysis cannot determine runtime heap adjacency.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 dynamic analysis: create a specific add/remove sequence, trigger the overflow, and dump heap state to determine which objects are corrupted

unresolved.description: Whether glibc 2.39 heap hardening (tcache key, safe-linking, chunk alignment checks) detects the corruption before it can be leveraged
unresolved.reason: glibc 2.39 has multiple heap consistency checks that may abort the process on detecting corrupted metadata. The overflow may trigger these checks during subsequent malloc/free operations.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 dynamic analysis: trigger the overflow and observe whether glibc aborts or allows continued execution with corrupted heap state

unresolved.description: Whether the info leak from puts() (BUG-002) produces useful address information or only leaks non-pointer heap data
unresolved.reason: The content adjacent to the message buffer depends on heap layout. If adjacent memory contains heap metadata with pointers (fd/bk in free chunks, or pointers in user structs), the leak is useful. If adjacent memory is mostly null or non-pointer data, the leak is not useful.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 dynamic analysis: fill a message buffer completely, call view, and examine the leaked output for address patterns
